userStories.title: Project setup and monorepo structure
userStories.description: Initialize the React Native (Expo bare or Expo managed) project and NestJS backend. Configure TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, and directory structure. Set up environment variable management.
acceptanceCriteria: React Native app runs on iOS simulator and Android emulator
NestJS backend starts with 'npm run start:dev'
TypeScript configured with strict mode in both app and backend
ESLint and Prettier pass with no errors
Environment variable templates (.env.example) exist for both app and backend
Basic README documents how to run both projects

userStories.title: Database schema — core tables
userStories.description: Create the PostgreSQL database schema with Drizzle ORM. Define all core tables: users, relationships, children, entries, entry_versions, attachments, acknowledgments, disputes, dispute_responses, audit_logs. Enforce immutability constraints at the schema level.
acceptanceCriteria: All tables defined in Drizzle schema files under src/database/schema/
users table: id (UUID), email, password_hash, display_name, timezone, default_currency, role (enum), created_at
relationships table: id, parent_a_id, parent_b_id (nullable), invite_token, invite_expires_at, created_at
children table: id, relationship_id, name, date_of_birth, created_at
entries table: id, relationship_id, child_id (nullable), type (enum: expense|event|agreement|communication|upload), created_by, created_at, status (enum: active|soft_deleted), current_version_id
entry_versions table: id, entry_id, version_number, content_json (JSONB), diff_json (nullable), created_by, created_at
attachments table: id, entry_version_id, original_filename, storage_path, file_hash (SHA-256 hex string), file_size_bytes, mime_type, uploaded_by, uploaded_at
acknowledgments table: id, entry_id, status (enum: pending|acknowledged|disputed), acted_by, created_at, comment (nullable)
disputes table: id, entry_id, raised_by, reason_text, created_at
dispute_responses table: id, dispute_id, responded_by, response_text, created_at
audit_logs table: id, user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, metadata_json, created_at
All created_at and uploaded_at columns use DEFAULT NOW() and are set server-side only
Drizzle migrations generated and applied to local dev database
No TypeScript errors in schema files

userStories.title: Authentication — registration and login
userStories.description: Implement user registration (email + password), email verification, and login with JWT. Password must be hashed with Argon2id. Auth guards applied to all protected routes.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/auth/register accepts email + password + display_name; creates user with password_hash (Argon2id); sends verification email
POST /v1/auth/verify-email accepts token from email; marks user as verified
POST /v1/auth/login accepts email + password; returns JWT access token and refresh token
POST /v1/auth/refresh accepts refresh token; returns new access token
POST /v1/auth/logout invalidates refresh token
Auth guard applied globally; @Public() decorator exempts public routes
Passwords never stored or returned in plaintext
Rate limiting applied to /register and /login (max 5 requests/min per IP)
All auth events logged to audit_logs
No TypeScript errors; unit tests for auth service pass

userStories.title: User profile and timezone/currency settings
userStories.description: Implement user profile API: get and update display name, timezone (IANA string), and default currency (ISO 4217). Timezone and currency are used for display formatting but all timestamps are stored in UTC.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /v1/users/me returns current user profile (id, email, display_name, timezone, default_currency, role)
PATCH /v1/users/me accepts display_name, timezone, default_currency; validates IANA timezone string and ISO 4217 code
Timezone stored as IANA string (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'Asia/Manila')
Currency stored as ISO 4217 code (e.g., 'USD', 'GBP', 'PHP')
Profile updates logged to audit_logs
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Co-parent invitation and relationship setup
userStories.description: Implement the invitation flow: Parent A invites Parent B via email. Parent B accepts (or declines) via a time-limited token link. Upon acceptance, a 'relationship' record is created linking both parents.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/relationships/invite accepts co-parent email; creates relationship record with parent_a_id set, parent_b_id null; sends invitation email with secure token
Invitation token expires after 7 days
POST /v1/relationships/accept accepts token; creates or links existing user account as parent_b; sets parent_b_id on relationship
GET /v1/relationships/me returns current user's relationship (status, co-parent display name, children)
POST /v1/relationships/invite/resend re-sends invitation email with new token if original expired
Invitation token is cryptographically random (not guessable)
Email sent via configured email provider (SendGrid or Postmark)
All invitation and acceptance events logged to audit_logs
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Children management
userStories.description: Implement CRUD for children within a relationship. Children are linked to a relationship_id and used to filter timeline entries. Only parents in the relationship can manage children.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/children accepts name and date_of_birth; creates child linked to current user's relationship
GET /v1/children returns all children for the current relationship
PATCH /v1/children/:id accepts name and date_of_birth updates
DELETE /v1/children/:id soft-deletes (sets deleted_at); child remains in historical entry records
Only users in the same relationship can view/manage children
Child creation and updates logged to audit_logs
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: File upload service with SHA-256 hashing
userStories.description: Implement file upload to S3-compatible storage. Every file is SHA-256 hashed during upload streaming. Hash is stored in the attachments table alongside file metadata. Files are stored encrypted at rest.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/uploads accepts multipart/form-data with a file; uploads to configured S3 bucket
SHA-256 hash computed during upload streaming (not from stored file); stored in attachments.file_hash
file_size_bytes, mime_type, original_filename, storage_path, uploaded_at stored on attachment record
Supported MIME types: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, application/pdf, video/mp4, video/quicktime
File size limit enforced: 50MB per file (configurable via env var)
Signed URLs returned for file access (time-limited: 15 minutes default)
Files stored in path format: uploads/{relationship_id}/{date}/{uuid}.{ext}
Upload events logged to audit_logs
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Entry creation — expense type
userStories.description: Implement the expense entry type. Expense entries capture: amount (integer in minor currency units), currency_code (ISO 4217), category, date, notes (optional), child_id (optional), and optional receipt file attachment. Every expense entry creates an entry_versions row as v1.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/entries/expense accepts: amount_minor_units (integer), currency_code, category, date, notes (optional), child_id (optional), attachment_id (optional from prior upload)
Creates entry record with type='expense', created_by, created_at (server-set)
Creates entry_versions record as version_number=1 with content_json containing all expense fields
If attachment_id provided, links attachment to entry_version_id
Entry status set to 'active'; acknowledgment status set to 'pending'
Creates acknowledgment record with status='pending'
Event logged to audit_logs
GET /v1/entries/:id returns entry with current version content and acknowledgment status
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Entry creation — event, agreement, communication, upload types
userStories.description: Implement the remaining 4 entry types using the same versioned entry architecture as expense. Each type has its own content_json schema.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/entries/event accepts: event_type (pickup|dropoff|activity|medical|school|other), assigned_parent_id, datetime, child_id, notes, attachment_id (optional); creates entry + v1 version + pending acknowledgment
POST /v1/entries/agreement accepts: description, effective_date, child_ids (array), notes; creates entry + v1 version; acknowledgment required from both parents before status='acknowledged'
POST /v1/entries/communication accepts: subject, body, child_id (optional), attachment_id (optional); creates entry + v1 version + pending acknowledgment
POST /v1/entries/upload accepts: attachment_id, description, child_id (optional); creates entry + v1 version + pending acknowledgment
All entry types use same entry + entry_versions + acknowledgments pattern
All entry creates logged to audit_logs
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Entry versioning — amend an entry
userStories.description: Implement the amend flow: a parent can amend an existing entry, which creates a new entry_versions row (not overwrite). The diff between versions is stored as diff_json. The original v1 is never modified.
acceptanceCriteria: PATCH /v1/entries/:id accepts updated content fields for the entry's type
Creates new entry_versions row: version_number = max(current) + 1, diff_json captures changed fields (old value → new value), created_by = requesting user, created_at = server-set
Updates entries.current_version_id to new version
Acknowledgment status reset to 'pending' on amendment
Amendment logged to audit_logs with diff summary
GET /v1/entries/:id/versions returns full version history in descending order (newest first)
Each version in history includes: version_number, created_by, created_at, diff_json
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Acknowledgment system
userStories.description: Implement the acknowledgment workflow: the co-parent can acknowledge or dispute any entry. Agreement entries require both parents to acknowledge before status moves to 'acknowledged'. All acknowledgment actions are immutable records.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/entries/:id/acknowledge creates acknowledgment record with status='acknowledged', acted_by, created_at (server-set), optional comment
POST /v1/entries/:id/dispute creates acknowledgment record with status='disputed', plus creates disputes record with reason_text
Acknowledgment action can only be taken by the co-parent (not the entry creator)
For agreement entries: entry status remains 'pending' until both parents have acknowledged
Acknowledgment and dispute events logged to audit_logs
GET /v1/entries/:id returns current acknowledgment status and timestamp
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Dispute response layer
userStories.description: Implement the dispute response flow: the entry creator can respond to a dispute with a written response and optional counter-evidence file. The full dispute thread (reason + response) is stored and included in exports.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/disputes/:id/respond accepts response_text and optional attachment_id; creates dispute_responses record
Only the entry creator can respond to their own entry's dispute
Counter-evidence attachment is hashed and stored the same as any other attachment
Dispute thread retrievable via GET /v1/entries/:id which includes nested disputes and responses
Dispute response logged to audit_logs
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Timeline feed API
userStories.description: Implement the timeline feed endpoint: paginated, cursor-based, chronological list of entries for the current relationship. Supports filtering by date range, child, entry type, and acknowledgment status.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /v1/timeline returns paginated list of entries (cursor-based pagination, default page size 20)
Each entry in response includes: id, type, created_by, created_at, current_version content summary, acknowledgment status, child name (if linked), attachment count
Query params: cursor (for pagination), child_id, type (multi-select), status (pending|acknowledged|disputed), from_date, to_date
Results ordered by created_at descending (newest first) by default
Response includes next_cursor for pagination
Only returns entries for the current user's relationship
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Push notifications — acknowledgment and entry alerts
userStories.description: Implement push notification delivery via Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) for Android and Apple Push Notification Service (APNs) for iOS. Notifications sent on: new entry by co-parent, acknowledgment received, dispute raised.
acceptanceCriteria: Mobile app registers device push token on login and stores it server-side
POST /v1/notifications/device-token accepts push token and platform (ios|android)
Notification sent within 60 seconds when co-parent creates a new entry
Notification sent within 60 seconds when an entry is acknowledged or disputed
Notification payload includes: entry type, entry date, action (new|acknowledged|disputed)
Tapping notification deep-links to the relevant entry in the app
Notification delivery failures do not break the entry creation flow (async, non-blocking)
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Mobile app — auth screens (login, register, verify email)
userStories.description: Build the authentication screens in React Native: registration form, login form, and email verification screen. Uses the auth API from story #3.
acceptanceCriteria: RegisterScreen: email, password, display name fields; submit calls POST /v1/auth/register; shows success message to check email
LoginScreen: email + password fields; submit calls POST /v1/auth/login; stores JWT in secure storage (expo-secure-store or equivalent)
VerifyEmailScreen: displayed after registration; shows instructions; 'Resend email' button
Auth state managed in global store (Zustand or context); redirects to main app on valid JWT
Loading states and error messages displayed for all API call states
Screens pass TypeScript type checks
Screens render correctly on iOS and Android

userStories.title: Mobile app — onboarding (invite co-parent, add children)
userStories.description: Build the onboarding flow for new users: invite co-parent by email, add first child. New users who haven't completed onboarding are shown this flow before the timeline.
acceptanceCriteria: InviteCoParentScreen: email input; submit calls POST /v1/relationships/invite; shows confirmation
AddChildScreen: name and date of birth fields; submit calls POST /v1/children; allows adding multiple children
Skip option available for both screens (user can complete later from settings)
Onboarding completion state tracked in user profile or local store
Users who receive an invitation see a 'Accept Invitation' flow after registration
Screens render correctly on iOS and Android
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Mobile app — timeline feed screen
userStories.description: Build the main Timeline screen in React Native. Displays the scrollable, paginated list of entries from GET /v1/timeline. Shows entry type, date, author, acknowledgment status badge, and child name.
acceptanceCriteria: TimelineScreen renders list of entries from GET /v1/timeline
Each entry row shows: entry type icon, date, author name, child name (if applicable), acknowledgment status badge (pending/acknowledged/disputed)
Infinite scroll: loads next page via cursor on scroll to bottom
Pull-to-refresh reloads timeline from beginning
Filter bar: filter by entry type (all/expense/event/agreement/communication/upload) and status (all/pending/disputed)
Empty state displayed when no entries
Tapping an entry navigates to EntryDetailScreen
Floating action button (FAB) opens entry type picker for creating a new entry
Neutral color scheme; no aggressive status colors
No TypeScript errors; renders on iOS and Android

userStories.title: Mobile app — entry detail screen
userStories.description: Build the EntryDetailScreen showing full entry content, version history, acknowledgment status, and the dispute thread. Actions: acknowledge, dispute, amend (if owner), view attachments.
acceptanceCriteria: EntryDetailScreen shows: entry type, full content (all fields), created_by, server-side created_at (formatted for user's timezone), child name, acknowledgment status
Acknowledgment section: if status=pending and current user is co-parent, show 'Acknowledge' and 'Dispute' buttons
Dispute section: if status=disputed, shows dispute reason; entry creator sees 'Add Response' button
Version history section: collapsible list of all versions (version number, created_at, who changed it, diff summary)
Attachments section: thumbnail/icon list of attached files; tap to view full file
Amend button visible only to entry creator; opens AmendEntrySheet
All timestamps displayed in user's configured timezone
No TypeScript errors; renders on iOS and Android

userStories.title: Mobile app — create entry screens (all 5 types)
userStories.description: Build the entry creation flows for all 5 entry types: expense, event, agreement, communication, upload. Each opens as a modal or bottom sheet from the timeline FAB. File picker integrated for receipt and attachment fields.
acceptanceCriteria: FAB on timeline opens entry type picker (bottom sheet): Expense, Event, Agreement, Communication, Upload
CreateExpenseSheet: amount field (numeric keypad), currency picker (defaults to user's preference), category picker, date picker, notes (optional), receipt photo button (camera or gallery)
CreateEventSheet: event type picker, assigned parent picker, date+time picker, child picker, notes (optional), attachment button
CreateAgreementSheet: description text area, effective date picker, child multi-select, notes (optional)
CreateCommunicationSheet: subject field, body text area, child picker (optional), attachment button
CreateUploadSheet: file picker (camera/gallery/file browser), description, child picker (optional)
File uploads trigger upload service (story #7) before entry submission; shows upload progress
All forms validate required fields before submission; inline error messages
Submission calls appropriate entry API endpoint; closes sheet on success; timeline refreshes
No TypeScript errors; works on iOS and Android

userStories.title: Court-ready PDF export generation
userStories.description: Implement the Timeline Report PDF export on the backend. Filterable by date range, child, and entry type. PDF is structured with labeled sections, chronological entries, inline attachment references, and a cover page with case metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/exports/pdf accepts filters: from_date, to_date, child_ids (array), entry_types (array)
PDF includes cover page: relationship metadata, export generated_at (UTC + user timezone), filter summary, total entry count
PDF sections in order: Summary, Expenses, Events, Agreements, Communications, Uploads, Disputes, Version History
Each entry row in PDF includes: entry ID, type, date (formatted), author, child (if applicable), status, acknowledgment timestamp (if applicable)
Dispute entries include: dispute reason, response (if any), timestamps
Attachments listed per entry with original filename and SHA-256 hash
PDF generated within 60 seconds for ≤500 entries
PDF returned as downloadable file (Content-Disposition: attachment)
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Evidence bundle ZIP export (PDF + JSON + attachments + hash manifest)
userStories.description: Implement the Evidence Bundle export: a ZIP file containing the PDF report, machine-readable JSON data, all relevant attachments, and a SHA-256 hash manifest file. This is the court-ready deliverable for lawyers.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /v1/exports/bundle accepts same filters as PDF export
ZIP contains: timeline-report.pdf, data.json, /attachments/ directory with all files, hash-manifest.txt
data.json is structured JSON with full entry data (all fields, all versions, all acknowledgments, all disputes) per the documented schema
hash-manifest.txt lists every file in /attachments/ with: original_filename, sha256_hash, upload_timestamp, entry_id
hash-manifest.txt includes plain-text verification instructions (how to run sha256sum to verify)
Attachment files in ZIP use original_filename (sanitized); collisions resolved with entry_id prefix
ZIP generated within 90 seconds for ≤500 entries
ZIP returned as downloadable file (Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=coparent-evidence-YYYYMMDD.zip)
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Mobile app — export screen
userStories.description: Build the Export screen in the mobile app. User configures filters (date range, children, entry types), triggers PDF or Evidence Bundle export, and downloads the result.
acceptanceCriteria: ExportScreen accessible from main navigation (tab or settings menu)
Date range picker: from_date and to_date
Child filter: multi-select from children in the relationship
Entry type filter: multi-select (all selected by default)
Two export buttons: 'Download PDF Report' and 'Download Evidence Bundle'
Loading state shown during export generation
On success: file saved to device or share sheet opened (platform-appropriate)
On error: clear error message displayed
No TypeScript errors; works on iOS and Android

userStories.title: Role-based access control and viewer role architecture
userStories.description: Implement the full role model: parent_a, parent_b, viewer. Viewer role is read-only and cannot create, edit, or acknowledge entries. Viewer access is grantable and revocable by either parent. All role assignments are logged.
acceptanceCriteria: Role enum in database: parent_a | parent_b | viewer
All entry creation, amendment, and acknowledgment endpoints reject viewer role with 403
POST /v1/relationships/viewers/invite accepts email; creates time-limited viewer access token (expires 30 days by default)
GET /v1/relationships/viewers returns list of current viewers (email, granted_at, expires_at)
DELETE /v1/relationships/viewers/:viewer_id revokes viewer access
Viewer can access GET /v1/timeline, GET /v1/entries/:id, GET /v1/children
Viewer cannot POST, PATCH, or DELETE any resource
All viewer grant/revoke events logged to audit_logs
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: i18n framework setup and locale support
userStories.description: Set up i18next (or equivalent) in the React Native app. Externalize all user-facing strings. Implement timezone-aware date/time display and locale-aware number/currency formatting. Phase 1 ships English only but architecture must support adding locales.
acceptanceCriteria: i18next (or react-i18next) installed and configured in React Native app
All user-facing strings in the app use t('key') translation calls; no hardcoded English strings
English translations in src/locales/en.json
All dates and times displayed using user's profile timezone (fetched from server)
All timestamps from server are UTC ISO 8601; converted to local timezone for display
Currency amounts formatted using Intl.NumberFormat with appropriate locale and currency code
Adding a new locale requires only a new JSON file in src/locales/ — no code changes
No TypeScript errors

userStories.title: Audit log completeness and security hardening
userStories.description: Ensure the audit_log table captures all significant system events. Add rate limiting to all sensitive endpoints. Verify no hard-delete paths exist. Run a security checklist against the auth and file storage implementations.
acceptanceCriteria: audit_logs entries exist for: user registration, login, profile update, relationship invite, child create/update/delete, entry create/amend, acknowledgment, dispute, dispute response, file upload, export generation, viewer grant/revoke
No DELETE SQL queries that hard-delete any entry, entry_version, attachment, or audit_log record
Rate limiting applied: POST /v1/auth/register and /v1/auth/login (5 req/min per IP), POST /v1/uploads (10 req/min per user), POST /v1/exports/* (3 req/min per user)
All API inputs validated with class-validator DTOs; no raw request body access
Signed URL expiry enforced at storage provider level (not just app level)
JWT secret loaded from environment variable; not hardcoded
No secrets in version control; .gitignore covers all .env files
Security checklist documented and signed off in SECURITY.md

userStories.title: End-to-end testing and pre-launch QA
userStories.description: Run end-to-end tests covering the core user journeys: registration → invite co-parent → add child → log expense → acknowledge → dispute → export PDF → export bundle. Verify hash manifest integrity. Fix all critical bugs.
acceptanceCriteria: E2E test: User A registers, invites User B, User B accepts; both users can see the same timeline
E2E test: User A logs an expense with a receipt; User B receives notification; User B acknowledges; both users see status='acknowledged'
E2E test: User A logs an event; User B disputes it; User A adds a counter-response; dispute thread is complete in both users' views
E2E test: User A generates PDF export; PDF contains all logged entries with correct content, timestamps, and hash references
E2E test: User A generates evidence bundle ZIP; hash manifest verifies correctly against extracted attachments using sha256sum
Version history test: User A logs expense, amends it twice; version history shows 3 versions with correct diffs
Security test: User A cannot access User C's (different relationship) entries; returns 403
Viewer test: Viewer can see timeline but cannot create or acknowledge entries
All tests pass on iOS simulator and Android emulator
No P0 or P1 bugs open at launch
